items.definition:
a member of a ship's or aircraft's crew
One of the crewmen was injured during the storm.

a raised platform for a speaker or performers
The speaker stood on the dais to address the audience.

lack of loyalty
His disloyalty to the company was evident.

a shapeless mass or blob of something
She added a dollop of cream to her coffee.

a small device that connects to a computer to provide it with additional functions
I need a USB dongle to connect my wireless mouse.

cloth hung in folds as a covering or decoration
The elegant drapery framed the large window.

a matted or ropelike strand of hair formed by braiding or locking
She had long dreadlocks that reached her waist.

an act or incident involving excitement, daring, or adventure
Their weekend escapade involved hiking and camping.

the state or quality of being final or complete
There was a sense of finality in his voice.

a house standing over or beside a gateway
The guard was stationed at the gatehouse.

a sweet, syrupy liquid used in medicines and cosmetics
This soap contains glycerin to moisturize the skin.

a rich source of something valuable
That old antique shop is a goldmine for collectors.

a keyboard instrument with plucked strings
The musician played a beautiful piece on the harpsichord.

a graphical representation of the distribution of numerical data
The data was presented as a histogram to show the frequency distribution.

Health Maintenance Organization
My health insurance plan is an HMO.

Individualized Education Program
Every student with special needs has an IEP.

a person who suffers from insomnia
As an insomniac, she often struggles to fall asleep at night.

the outline of the lower jaw
He had a strong, defined jawline.

a fertile soil of clay and sand containing humus
The garden thrived in the rich loam.

a woman who gives massages
She booked an appointment with the masseuse.

a person who makes a mess or does things badly
He's a real messer when it comes to cooking.

a device used by musicians that marks time at a selected rate by giving a regular tick
The pianist practiced with a metronome to keep time.

the middle part of a range or scale
The company offers a wide range of products, from entry-level to high-end, with a strong focus on the midrange.

a small freshwater fish; an unimportant person or thing
The team was considered a minnow in the league, but they surprised everyone with their performance.

a pearly white or bluish gemstone
She wore a beautiful necklace with a polished moonstone pendant.

Not in Education, Employment, or Training
The government is trying to reduce the number of NEETs by offering more vocational training programs.

a drink, especially eggnog
We enjoyed a warm glass of eggnog by the fireplace during the holidays.

energy, enthusiasm, or sex appeal
The new marketing campaign needs more oomph to attract customers.

a common person; a member of the lower classes
He dismissed their concerns, treating them like mere plebs.

the act of appearing again
His sudden reappearance surprised everyone.

any disease marked by inflammation and pain in the joints, muscles, or fibrous tissue
My grandmother suffers from rheumatism in her knees.

the quality of being unselfish; concern for others
Her selflessness was evident in her dedication to charity work.

mushroom (informal)
He found a big shroom growing in the forest.

a sequence of drawings representing the shots planned for a film or television production
The director reviewed the storyboard before filming began.

a term of endearment; a sweet food item (UK)
Come here, sweety, and give me a hug.

a unit or formation temporarily organized to carry out a specific mission
The government formed a taskforce to address the housing crisis.

a digital record of the time of occurrence of a particular event or action
The video has a timestamp showing when it was recorded.

the state of being disliked or not admired
The politician's unpopularity grew after the scandal.

the speed of an aircraft relative to the air through which it is moving
The pilot checked the airspeed before takeoff.

the use of aromatic plant extracts and essential oils for healing and cosmetic purposes
She uses aromatherapy to relax after a long day.

a sloping surface or edge
The carpenter cut a perfect bevel on the edge of the wood.

an exclamation of approval, especially for a female performer
The audience shouted 'Brava!' after her solo.

A heavy, stout shoe
He wore sturdy brogans for the long hike.

A word or phrase, often jargon, that is fashionable at a particular time
Synergy became a popular buzzword in the 1990s.

A person who has been shipwrecked and stranded in an isolated place
The novel tells the story of a lone castaway on a deserted island.

A sharp, abrupt sound, especially one made by two hard objects striking together
The old typewriter made a satisfying clack with every key press.

A person who is compelled to serve in the armed forces
The army relied heavily on conscripts during the war.

A crease or series of creases in something, especially hair or fabric
She put a crimp in her hair for the party.

the process of making something inactive
The deactivation of the alarm system was successful.

the style and arrangement of decoration
The restaurant had a modern décor.

a woman who uses magic or charms
The story featured a powerful enchantress.

a thing that is unpleasant or ugly to look at
That abandoned building is a real eyesore.

a confrontation or dispute; (in sports) a method of starting play
The two teams prepared for the faceoff.

a small mechanical or electronic device or gadget
He loves playing with all the latest electronic gizmos.

a sticky, slimy, or messy substance
The baby got goop all over his face.

a woman who hunts
Artemis was the Greek goddess of the hunt and a skilled huntress.

the policy or practice of providing equal access to opportunities and resources for people who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized
The company strives for greater inclusiveness in its hiring practices.

a length of timber or steel supporting part of the structure of a building, typically arranged in parallel series to support a floor or ceiling
The floor joists were rotten and needed to be replaced.

a type of floor covering
The kitchen floor was covered with old linoleum.

a stringed musical instrument
Ancient Greek poets often played the lyre while reciting their verses.

one millionth of a gram
The dosage was only a few micrograms.

a wrong calculation or judgment
The project failed due to a serious miscalculation in the budget.

the act of misleading someone
The magician used misdirection to distract the audience.

discussion, negotiation
The two sides agreed to hold a parley to discuss the terms of peace.
